page_metadata.title: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling of human exposure to perfluorooctanoic acid suggests historical non drinking-water exposures are important for predicting current serum concentrations

model_classification.evidence_quote: The objective of this research is to apply physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling and Monte Carlo analysis to evaluate the impact of historic non-drinking water PFOA exposure on serum PFOA concentrations.

model_context.model_origin: scaled from previously published PFOA rat PBPK models to adult humans
model_context.stated_purpose: Evaluate historical non-drinking-water PFOA exposure and explain current human serum PFOA concentrations using PBPK and Monte Carlo analysis

stated_assumptions.description: Cardiac output and rate constants are body-weight scaled.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: The human model was developed with body-weight scaling for physiological flows and rate constants.

stated_assumptions.description: Renal handling includes basolateral and apical transporter processes.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: blood→proximal tubule cells by basolateral transport ... filtrate→PT cells by apical Michaelis-Menten transport

stated_assumptions.description: Historical non-drinking-water ingestion is included as an exposure source.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: Simulation ... successfully predicted 98% of individual serum PFOA concentrations ... when non-drinking water ingestion of PFOA exposure was included.

absorption.evidence_quote: PFOA enters through drinking-water and non-drinking-water oral exposure; gastric and intestinal absorption are modeled.

elimination.evidence_quote: Urinary, biliary and fecal elimination are modeled; renal handling includes active transport and reabsorption.

unresolved.description: kdif is described in the kidney model but is not numerically tabulated in the main chemical-specific parameter table.
unresolved.reason: Named model parameter without a numerical value in Table 2.

allometric_scaling_rules: k0c, kabsc, kunabsc, keffluxc, kbilec, kurinec and gastric emptying rate scaled as BW^-0.25

verification.summary: Updated audited extraction: retains direct Table 1/Table 2 model values, flags the log-scale Monte Carlo table, keeps kdif unquantified, and moves drinking-water concentrations out of dosing because they are exposure concentrations.

flags.message: Table 3 lognormal means/SDs/bounds are on the log scale and are not direct parameter values.
kdif is named in the kidney model narrative but no numerical value is reported in Table 2.
Drinking-water concentrations are exposure concentrations, not administered dose amounts; they are retained as exposure-scenario findings.
